POLICY GOVERNING USE OF RECREATIONAL FACILITIES The purpose of this Policy (hereinafter “Policy”) is to establish the rules and conditions under which Town recreational facilities (hereinafter “Facilities”) may be used by outside agencies, individuals and groups. ELIGIBLE USERS

A. Category A Users:

- 1. Governmental agencies, such as local municipal, county, State, and

Federal agencies.

- 2. Public meetings sponsored by governmental agencies involving government projects including, but not limited to, planned unit development reviews and public notices.

- 3. State universities and colleges and community colleges, and public schools located in Harris County, Georgia.

- 4. Athletic, recreation, or other programs directly administered, sponsored, or supported by local governmental agencies that are not created or used for personal or financial gain.

B. Category B Users:

Not-for-profit organizations qualified under State or Federal Jaw, student groups, parent groups and clubs not sponsored by the Town which meet the following criteria:
1:
They primarily serve residents of the Town;

Their primary aim is the development of educational, athletic, social or self-improvement skills;

They charge no fees other than membership dues and costs of any supplies consumed in the program;

The organizers, supervisors, administrators are unpaid volunteers, provided that umpires and referees may be paid for sporting events; and

They have signed a certification form stating that the organization meets all requirements to qualify as a Category B User.

Category C Users:

Any other not-for-profit organizations or groups, other student groups and clubs and parent groups that do not qualify as a Category A or B users.

Any Category B User when:

- a. conducting fund-raising events, and when less than 100% of the gross receipts are retained by or provided to the Town; or, b. performing certain fund-raising activities, such as:

- (1) charging for admission, soliciting contributions for admission, or requiring any tangible thing of value to participate in the activity for which the Facility is being requested; or,

- (2) ‘requiring any donation of money or other tangibles of monetary value; or,

- (3) _ selling or bartering any tangible thing of monetary value.

Facility Use Waivers:

Prospective Users who do not fall within the use categories defined herein may request a waiver in writing for use of Town Facilities from the Mayor. Once a use waiver approval is granted by the Mayor for a prospective User, any and all a a ear approval may, however, be revoked by the Mayor at any time and for any reason.

The Mayor and-Council shall develop and approve a schedule of fees for the use of the Facilities. The Mayor may adopt changes to the schedule of fees as appropriate. The schedule of fees shall consider costs associated with the use of the Facilities such as, custodial services, energy consumption, maintenance, and repair. The schedule of fees shall be applied to the categories of

Users as follows:

A. Category A and B Users:

No rental fee shall be charged to Category A or Category B Users, however, applicable Securify, custodial, audio-visual (“A/V”) technician and other fees shall be charged.

B. Category C User:

A fee shall be charged based on rental rates approved by the Mayor, including any applicable custodial, A/V technician and other fees.

C. Fee Waivers:

Users granted a Use Waiver shall be charged as a Category C Users. Waivers of fees shall not be granted unless recommended and approved by the Mayor. Fee Waiver requests must be submitted at least thirty (30) days in advance of the dates of the dates of desired use in order to provide sufficient time for action by the

Mayor.
6: The following apply to all categories of Users except where indicated.
7:
Town personnel, custodians, or approved volunteers may be present at any time a

Facility is being used.

All Users must complete and submit a Use Agreement and do so at least ten (10) working days prior to the requested date. Use Agreements are available at City Hall. Use requests will include details regarding the purpose of the requested use, date(s) and hours requested, and the specific Facilities requested. Tax-exempt numbers must be provided when claiming tax-exempt status.

Any fees must be paid seven (7) business days in advance. Any payments made less than seven (7) business days, must be in the form of a cashier’s check or money order. Any other billing arrangements must be approved by the Mayor.

Cancellation notice must be given by Users at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance. In the event of any cancellation, consideration of any refund shall be at the discretion of the Mayor. The Town reserves the right to charge an administrative fee to Users that cancelled a Use Agreement and submitted another Use Agreement within thirty (30) days of the given cancellation. The Town shall not be liable or responsible for any delays or cancellations due to strikes, riots, acts of God, shortages of labor or materials (including but not limited to the unavailability of a Town A/V technician), national emergency, acts of a public enemy, governmental restrictions, laws, or regulations.

All Users must provide reasonable supervision and shall be financially liable for all damage to Facilities resulting from their use.

All Users must assume all liability, provide proof of liability insurance, and shall indemnify hold the Town harmless for any and all damages or injuries that result

from any use of the Facilities, including, without limitation, any and all liability and costs arising from injury to persons or property occasioned wholly or in part by any act or omission of the User, its employees, members, invitees, and all other persons whom the User permits in, on, or about the Facilities. The User shall defend any and all claims, actions, suits, or legal proceedings which may be brought against the Town or any officer or agent thereof, or in which the Town or any officer or agent thereof may be impleaded or joined with others as a result of the user’s use of the Facilities or property designated herein, and shall satisfy and discharge any judgments, orders, and decrees that may be recovered against the user or the Town or any officer or agent thereof, in any such action or proceedings. Users understand and agree that the foregoing indemnification shall not constitute a waiver of the Town’s sovereign immunity under Georgia law.

At all times material to any Use Agreement, Users provide general liability insurance covering bodily injury and property damage arising from use of the Facilities. This coverage shall have limits $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate. The Town must be identified as a certificate holder and shall be named as an additional insured. The User shall present proof of such insurance which must contain a clause requiring the insurer to provide the Town with thirty (30) days written notice prior to the cancellation of such insurance for any reason.

Users will be responsible for any and all damages to or theft of Town property and shall reimburse the Town in an amount determined by the Mayor in accordance with established accounting principles. Failure to reimburse the Town shall automatically disqualify the User from any further use of Facilities.

Users shall be responsible for supervising the conduct and control of all patrons and participants while on the premises of the Facilities, and shall ensure that all applicable laws and Town policies and procedures are strictly obeyed.

Violation of this Policy, or any other applicable Town policy or procedure during the use of Town Facilities, may subject the User to immediate revocation of the

Use Agreement and refusal of permission to use Facilities in the future.

Any User required to obtain a State or Municipal license must:

- 1. Provide a copy of same to the Town; 2. Ensure that all persons served by a user must be officially enrolled in their program.

The right of use by any User required to obtain a license is subject to cancellation if they do not meet the State or Municipal standards or requirements.

Users of Facilities must take responsibility for safety when dangerous lightning weather conditions are present. Users of outdoor Facilities (fields, courts, playground areas etc.) must cease activities, vacate the area, and take appropriate safe shelter in available buildings and/or vehicles if (1) lightning is seen, (2) thunder is heard, or (3) the Town’s weather warning system is activated. In the event that lightning was seen or thunder was heard, Users may resume outdoor activities on Facilities only after the dangerous weather conditions have cleared the area.

Any User of indoor Facilities where fifty (50) people or more will be present must have a trained crowd manager present and comply with the published crowd management and fire safety requirements of the fire safety codes of the Town and the state of Georgia.

As determined by the Mayor, a security deposit may be required for the following reasons, including but not limited to, past damage to Town equipment or property, or excessive cleaning and debris removal. Users required to pay a security

deposit must submit a check fifteen (15) business days in advance of the lease event; the check shall be made payable to: “The Town of Pine Mountain”. Any damages in excess of the amount of the deposit will be billed to the User. The security deposit will be refunded upon satisfactory inspection of the Facility.
8: The following restrictions apply to all categories of Users.
9:
Users must comply with all applicable Town policies and procedures, including this Policy and all safety and security procedures applicable to all Facilities.

Users shall not: (1) use, remove, reposition, replace, move, or otherwise disturb any Town equipment or property; or (2) make any physical changes to the

Facilities buildings or grounds.

Users shall not tamper with or adjust any security, fire protection equipment, fire alarms, intercoms, thermostats, light or air conditioning timers, or any other electrical, communication, or control systems.

The consumption of alcoholic beverages, use of illegal drugs, and carrying of firearms (except by law enforcement personnel) are all strictly prohibited. All property owned by the Town, including all interior and exterior spaces within the property boundaries, shal! be smoke and tobacco free.

Users shall not store anything on Town property. Users acknowledge that anything stored or left on Town property, may be confiscated and disposed of and that additional charges may be assessed. Users must make reasonable efforts to clean rooms and areas used or return them to their pre-use condition.

Blocking of fire doors or means of egress is prohibited.

~

G. Users will not attempt to assign any Use Agreement or otherwise sublet the

Facilities or allow any use other than that for which approved.

H. Users shall not produce an open flame(s) (e.g., the burning of candles is prohibited). PROHIBITED USES A. Facilities shall not be used by any organization, group, or entity that discriminates on the basis of race, color, sex, age, religion, disability, national origin, marital status, or any other protectable classification under federal or state law.

B. Facilities may not be used by businesses or private individuals for personal or private financial gain.

C. Facilities shall not be used for any use inconsistent with Town Ordinances, this

Policy or State, and Federal law.

D. Facilities shall not be used for any activity which would have the effect of damaging said Facilities or associated grounds beyond normal wear and tear or for any activity which would interfere with Town activities or operations.

RESOLUTION CREATING A PUBLIC RECREATION BOARD FOR THE TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN, GEORGIA

BE IT RESOLVED by the Mayor and Town Council of the Town of Pine

Mountain, Georgia:

Under the provisions of Georgia laws 1946, pages 152-154, and Georgia jaws 1971, p 262, there is hereby established the Pine Mountain Parks and Recreation Board. This Board shail be appointed by the Mayor and Town Council of Pine Mountain, Georgia, and shail consist of Five (5) persons, serving without pay. Their terms of office of the members of the Board shall be for five (5) years or until their successors are appointed and qualified, except that the membership of such Board first appointed shall be appointed for such terms that the term of one member shall expire annualiy hereafter. Vacancies in such Board occurring otherwise than by expiration of term shall be filled by another appointment for the unexpired tern. Those appointed to this Public Recreation Board and their terms of office are; Roger Childers, 5 years: Brent Bullington, 4 years: Chad Kimbrough, 3 years: James Copeland, Z years: and Angei Culp, 1 year. Consultants to this Board, to work hand-in-hand with the board, shall also serve five year terms and work under the same restrictions and liberties as the Board. The Consultants shall be appointed by the Mayor and Town Council of the Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia, and shall consist of six (6) persons, to serve without pay. Those appointed as Consultants to the Public Recreation Board and their terms of office are: Bill Champion, 5 years: Jerry Armstrong,

5 years: Mike King, 4 years: Butch McGuire, 3 years: Sandra Williams, Z years: and Nonie Lott, 1 year.

Immediately hereafter the membership shali meet and organize by electing one of their members chairman, and such other officers as they deem necessary. The Board and Consultants shall recommend for adoption by the Mayor and Town Council of Pine Mountain such by-laws, rules and regulations for the proper conduct of said Board.

The Public Recreation Board and Consultants shall provide, conduct and supervise public playgrounds, playfields, recreation centers and other recreational facilities owned or controlled by the Town or as may hereafter be acquired by the Town. Said Board shall have the power to conduct any form of recreation, cultural or sports activity that will employ the leisure time of the people in 3 wholesome or constructive manner. It may conduct such activities on property under its own control, on public properties with the consent of the authorities thereof and on private properties with the consent of the owners.

- 4. From time to time the Board shall recommend to the Mayor and Council of Pine Hountain recommendations for employment of trained or properly qualified persons for the work and activities of said Board.

S. Any expenditure of funds by ssid Board shall be upon 2 properly submitted budget epproved by the Mayor and Council of Pine Mountain. The Board may aiso solicit or receive any gifts, grants, or bequests of money or other personal or real property on behalf of or in the name of Pine Mountain, or any donation to be spplied, principal or income, for either temporary or permanent use for park or recreational purposes.

- 6. Said Board shall make an annual, comprehensive, narrative progress report, inciuding financial statements, if any, to the Mayor and Council, and such other reports as may from time to time be required.

- 2. This resolution does not provide the Board with any power to incur any bonded or other indebtedness or to levy taxes for any purpose.
